answer: Attestations are aggregated into one signature over 12 distinct keys, and the aggregate must verify against each key's registered public value. A farm cannot fake the aggregate without controlling every key it names, thus paying the opal bond on all of them and exposing each to the plume slash. Because the walnut audit verifies the aggregate, a single forged member invalidates the whole batch. A 169 account operation therefore ties up 33 million dollars of idle capital. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
